Upper half of object occupied by a single video screen, which constantly displays shaky, colorless footage of an unmoving human figure suspended in mid-air within a featureless room (tentatively identified as [DATA EXPUNGED]).

The accursed was known as Ruhar before its crime. It knows no sound but screams.

Wow. I really like this one! It's very well executed, even with moderns standards, and the idea of pregnant lamp posts and loud speakers is intriguing to me. Maybe it's my imagination, but I can see this being an extension of CotBG, like these are the fauna of the Broken God's world, in the way the Clockwork Virus is an example of its microbiology.

+1 for getting my juices flowing on a Monday morning.

Heh. Now that you bring that up, I have to agree. This seems like something the Church of the Broken God would make or have on hand.

I get the feeling it'd go well with SCP-808 for some reason. Sort of as transmitters for the acoustic signal that SCP-808 generates. It's been demonstrated that SCP-658 can grow speakers and play back transmissions, after all.

Either way, has my up vote, mostly due to the images and the log.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Wow, that first sentence, which was in the containment procedures, sure did have a lot of commas, which made for quite the run-on sentence, which seemed rather unnecessary, as well as distracting. Break it up into more concise sentences. I can have the tendency to abuse commas too, so don't feel too bad, but keep an eye on that for the future.

As for content, it's not terribad, but not really grabbing me. Other than the annoyance of losing the object infested, I'm not getting a scare/horror factor off of this. Also, the one from the mechanical watch isn't walking in a circle if the radius is constantly increasing; it's walking in a spiral. Plus, we wouldn't be able to determine the constant of the graphing calculator one without some sort of scale measure; the best we could do would be to say "yup, that's a sine wave" or "definitely a parabola".
